title: Resilient tenant-aware reorder buffer and commit coordinator for structured log ingress
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: Our current ingress pipeline occasionally delivers out-of-order or duplicated structured log chunks for multi-tenant traffic under transient Kafka rebalances and downstream sink pressure. This leads to incorrect user-visible timelines in dashboards and intermittent alert noise for customers on Dedicated. Goal: Implement a tenant-scoped reorder buffer and commit coordinator that guarantees per-tenant monotonic commit visibility to downstream consumers (Loki/ELK/backends) without significantly raising tail latency for healthy paths.
proposal: Introduce a lightweight per-tenant reordering buffer that uses monotonic sequence numbers assigned at the ingress gateway, durable anchoring for in-flight batches (rocksdb-backed index), and a distributed commit coordinator that reconciles commit offsets. Key pieces: (1) assign tenant-seq on entry and surface idempotency token; (2) buffer small windows (configurable, default 2s/1k events) to reorder late-arriving fragments; (3) durable anchor + commit log for at-most-once visibility to downstream; (4) backpressure signals to upstream producers and dynamic window shrink under high memory/latency; (5) fast-path bypass for low-latency tenants when reordering not needed.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No >1 minute timeline inversion observed in canary tenant for 7-day test. 2) End-to-end p99 ingest latency increases by <15% for non-reordered tenants. 3) Reordering correctness verified by synthetic test harness comparing original event timestamps and visible commits. 4) Feature toggles allow immediate rollback to current path without data loss. 5) New metrics emitted: tenant_reorder_window_ms, tenant_reorder_commits, tenant_reorder_dropped, tenant_reorder_memory_bytes.
rollout_plan: Phase A: Unit + integration tests + internal staging run with 3 tenants (7d). Phase B: Canary to 5% traffic (non-critical tenants) for 72h, monitor dashboards/alerts. Phase C: Gradual ramp to 50% and then 100% for telemetry-ingest. At each step, automated smoke tests validate ordering and drop rates. Rollback via runtime flag to bypass reorder buffer and replay using durable anchor for uncommitted windows.
tradeoffs: - Durable anchoring (rocksdb) increases local disk usage but reduces lost-in-flight risk. - Short buffer windows favor latency over correctness; long windows favor correctness at expense of tail latency. We choose adaptive windows. - Coordinating commits adds complexity and new failure modes; mitigated via leaderless fallback where the ingress service falls back to timestamp-based ordering if coordinator unavailable.
testing: Unit tests for sequence assignment and idempotency, integration harness that replays interleaved partitions and simulated rebalances, chaos test: kill coordinator leader during in-flight windows, soak test: 48h steady high-throughput with synthetic tenant traffic, performance benchmark against current path to quantify p50/p95/p99.
qa_tasks: Create synthetic tenant workloads in staging and record baseline ordering violations
Run coordinator failover scenarios and verify no duplicate commits
Validate Grafana panels show expected metrics and no alert flapping
